vendor: Updated `k8s.io/system-validators` to `v1.12.1`. The cgroups validator now throws an error instead of a warning if cgroups v1 is detected on the host and the provided KubeletVersion is `v1.35` or newer.

During `kubeadm init`, `kubeadm join`, and `kubeadm upgrade`, the SystemVerification preflight check throws an error if cgroups v1 is detected and the detected `kubelet` version is `v1.35` or newer. For older versions of `kubelet`, a preflight warning is displayed.

To allow cgroups v1 with `kubeadm` and `kubelet` version `v1.35` or newer, you must:
- Ignore the error from the SystemVerification preflight check by `kubeadm`.
- Edit the `kube-system/kubelet-config` ConfigMap and add the `failCgroupV1: false` field before upgrading.

issueContext.title: remove rsync from build
issueContext.body:
There's a _lot_ of complexity in the build system around rsync + build + data containers.

This was mostly added to work around docker desktop filesystem performance on macOS, but also used to support building against docker on a remote VM.

Besides the docker desktop licensing changes probably reducing how many developers are actually using docker desktop, it's not clear that we should still be jumping through this many hoops in the build.

OTOH, removing it may be fairly involved, and it's possible the performance gap is still substantial, even if using filesystem caching (which appears to be replaced now https://github.com/docker/for-mac/issues/5402).

We should test performance and weigh ripping this stuff out to simplify the build.

cc @thockin @cblecker

/sig release

This issue was reported in the [Kubernetes 1.24 Security Audit Report](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-security/blob/main/sig-security-external-audit/security-audit-2021-2022/findings/Kubernetes%20v1.24%20Final%20Report.pdf)

**Impact**
A misconfiguration of the API server could lead to a situation where privilege escalation for
any authenticated user to cluster admin is possible.

**Description**
The Kubernetes API server allows a certificate authority (CA) to be specified (using the `--
client-ca-file flag`) which will be used to verify client certificates under the familiar X.
509 client certificate authentication scheme6. Another CA can be specified (using `--
requestheader-client-ca-file`) that will be used to verify requests authenticated using
the request header scheme (described in the documentation as Authenticating Proxy). If
these two CAs are the same, and the `--requestheader-allowed-names` flag is not used to
specify particular certificate common names that are permitted for request header
authentication, it is possible for any holder of a client certificate from the shared CA to
trivially authenticate to the API server as any user, by using their certificate to authenticate
a request using the request header scheme. While it is not intended that these CAs be the
same, and common Kubernetes deployment methods do not configure the deployment in
this way, it is possible that administrators could be unaware of this pitfall.

The Kubernetes documentation does include some advice against sharing CAs, but is not
explicit about the potentially serious security impact of this specific case.

For an example, please see the original finding on page 18 of the [Kubernetes 1.24 Security Audit Report](https://github.com/kubernetes/sig-security/blob/main/sig-security-external-audit/security-audit-2021-2022/findings/Kubernetes%20v1.24%20Final%20Repo

### What happened? There is a bug in `kubelet` `startupProbe` if sidecar container is configured. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.32/pkg/kubelet/prober/worker.go#L249 The worker's decision to continue (return true) or stop (return false) is based only on the pod's restart policy, not the containers (sidecar have restartPolicy:Always) This can lead to a racing condition if the sidecar container fails at the first time and prober incorrectly exits: If sidecar container restarted with no problem at second attempt, startupProbe will never run again. However if there are more than one containers has startup probes, and the first container has a running probe, it will skip other containers (because of an early`return`). issueContext.title: Confusing use of TooManyRequests error for eviction
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

When the Kubernetes API server returns a 429 (throttled), the response may include misleading cause information.

We observed that a pod eviction API call received a response that included _**both**_ of the following fragments:

``` json
"responseStatus": {
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "reason": "TooManyRequests",
  "code": 429
},
```

and

``` json
"responseObject": {
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "Cannot evict pod as it would violate the pod's disruption budget.",
  "reason": "TooManyRequests",
  "details": {
    "causes": [
      {
        "reason": "DisruptionBudget",
        "message": "The disruption budget [elided] needs 11 healthy pods and has 12 currently"
      }
    ]
  },
  "code": 429
},
```
Note that the `message` given above is confusing, as there are more currently healthy pods than the required number.


### What did you expect to happen?

When a request is rejected due to throttling (429 HTTP response), either
* no other error information should be included; or
* the included error information should indicate throttling

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Provoke a 429 HTTP response and inspect the response.

Issue #88535 seems to be similar - it also describes a 429 response where inclusion of a cause resulted in confusion.

issueContext.title: AssumeCache may detect the PersistentVolume update later than the scheduler's event handlers
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

Let's say we have a scenario where Pod is rejected waiting for a PersistentVolume to be available.
When the PersistentVolume status is updated to `Available`, the scheduler is notified via event handlers.

One of such handlers, in [eventhandling.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18c188467d8ae00042b61f82aa159094336b657e/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L566) is responsible for triggering the Pod's scheduling retry. In this case, the reason is valid, so the Pod is placed in the activeQ (or backoffQ) and then taken to the scheduling.

However, during the (pre)filtering of VolumeBinding plugin, the PersistentVolume objects are [listed](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18c188467d8ae00042b61f82aa159094336b657e/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/binder.go#L825) from the plugin's AssumeCache, which have its own set of the [event handlers](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18c188467d8ae00042b61f82aa159094336b657e/pkg/scheduler/util/assumecache/assume_cache.go#L208-L214). If these handlers receive the PV update event later than the main scheduler's handlers, VolumeBinding takes the decision based on an old data, e.g. a PersistentVolume with an old state. As a result, the Pod is [rejected](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18c188467d8ae00042b61f82aa159094336b657e/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/volumebinding/binder.go#L885) and goes back to the scheduling queue.

issueContext.title: Preemption process does not leave a trait in the scheduler cache causing a race
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

The preemption process that is initiated by the scheduler does not leave the immediate trait in the cache. Due to a race, a pod may come back to the scheduling queue before the in-memory state gets updated (receives a notification about a pod being deleted or marked for deletion DeletionTimestamp != nil) and start the same preemption process again.

Whenever the preemption process identifies a pod eligible for preemption, but learns the pod does no longer exist, it immediately puts the preemptor back to scheduling queue (since it may never receive a notification that wakes it up from the unschedulable queue) and the process repeats in a tight loop, each time producing a pod delete api call.

The factor that triggers this issue is the fact that when a pod being preempted is in the binding process, the scheduler lets it finish the process and IGNORES pod delete notifications, waiting for this async binding process to fail. This creates quite a wide window making the problem very likely to happen in a specific use case, like autoscaling when initial pods jump into nodes they were not intended to and need to be preempted right after). Large number of outgoing api-calls (to delete non-existing pod) generates a big load on the api-server and may generate a snowball effect.

The issue itself exists from a long time, but the PR which closed the loop by activating preemptor pod on failure was added to 1.34 https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/133213

### What did you expect to happen?

The information about a non-existing pod should be reflected in the in-memory cache to cut that loop.

It could be either recorded right after pod delete was accepted or even better whenever any attempt to delete it failed (non-existing pod)

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

issueContext.title: Kubelet rejects pod with "NodeAffinity failed" due to stale informer data
issueContext.body:
#### What happened

This issue is similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/100467 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92067.

We have a controller that adds labels to a node after it starts up. It looks like there are cases where the scheduler is able to see the new node labels and schedule a pod, but the kubelet somehow doesn't see the new labels - it has stale data in its informer cache. Whatever the reason for the stale data, the result is that the kubelet rejects the pod with "NodeAffinity failed".

#### What did you expect to happen

Kubelet to be able to detect the new node labels and not reject the pod. 

The only reason that we need to keep the node affinity / node selector check in the kubelet is in case someone sets `nodeName` directly on the pod, so that it does not go through the scheduler, so we can't just remove enforcement on the node level.

The short-term fix would be for the kubelet to synchronously fetch the node object when (and only when) it sees these "NodeAffinity failed" errors and try again. To ensure we do not introduce additional heavy traffic when there many pods being scheduled at once, we will have to keep a new cache, separate from the informer cache. The logic would be like:
- Read the node object from the informer
- If we get a NodeAffinity failed error, read the node object from our new cache
- If we still get a NodeAffinity failed error, fetch the node object synchronously from the api server
The cache should be updated whenever we see a node object that is newer than the one we are currently storing - this can come from either the informer or from the synchronous fetch.

issueContext.title: No share ID in DRA kubelet plugin's API
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

kubelet plugin API does not support ShareID information. The ShareID is an additional identifier to the device name which may be generated by DRAConsumableCapacity feature ( that is introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5104). 

The DRA driver which refers to this API for preparing resource needs to pass ShareID to CDI spec's device ID. Otherwise, the same node will fail to create a container according to the duplicate ID. 



### What did you expect to happen?

Pods can be successfully created when sharing the same device with DRAConsumableCapacity.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Enable DRAConsumableCapacity feature, Enable DRA driver with allowMultipleAllocations device, Create two pods allocating the same device.

### Anything else we need to know?

Without the change to k/k, a driver can have a workaround which wrap the plugin API appending with shareID and use it as a PreparedDevice.

From 
```go
type PreparedDevice struct {
	Device         DRADevice
	ContainerEdits *cdiapi.ContainerEdits
}
```
to
```go
type DRADevice struct {
	drapbv1.Device
	shareID *types.UID
}
type PreparedDevice struct {
	Device         DRADevice
	ContainerEdits *cdiapi.ContainerEdits
```

issueContext.title: APF significantly under-reporting seats for watches without RV
issueContext.body: From a recent study, we observed API server’s CPU usage (on a 96 vCPU instance) vs "current_executing_seats" was extremely skewed: Computing the CPU usage/seat during that time, it swings quite a bit (0.4-2.0): For that period in the middle where CPU usage/seat is relatively high, majority of the seat usage comes from "workload-low" priority level: Dissecting it further, we can correlate the usage to watch calls from a particular client: These were all watches with RV unset (could've also been RV set to 0): Such calls are expensive upfront due to initial "Add" events being generated for the entire collection, as required by our [API semantics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/using-api/api-concepts/#semantics-for-watch). **So why do they have such low seat usage?** The API server's seat calculation logic intends to count watch calls that don't need to send init events at the lowest cost. It does this by checking SendInitialEvents parameter isn't set to true ([xref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0f8471a6f5b00e93409422f1a39e4655651c105a/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/request/list_work_estimator.go#L91-L95)). But that misses the RV unset/0 cases (i.e. legacy watches), under reporting their penalty too. We need to exclude those from incorrectly being assigned minimum seats.

**Is this a BUG REPORT or FEATURE REQUEST?**:

Nodes does not change their own ip that frequent on `azure` or any cloud/om-prem deployment for that matter. Once the cluster burns through the quota its control plane will become practically unusable until quota refill, refresh or manual shutdown/start of controller to slow down the calls.

`Route Controller` must generate the smallest possible of cloud calls. Ideally, only when needed. And must be reasonably fast in reaction to changing state such as `new nodes`, `deleted nodes`, or changing `node ip`

issueContext.title: Codify inter-FeatureGate dependencies
issueContext.body:
It's becoming increasingly common to add new feature gates for extensions on features that still have a feature gate. Today we handle this in an ad-hoc way, where we sometimes check both feature gates (the one directly controlling the new extension, and the one for the original feature), but in lots of cases we just check the direct feature gate.

Rather than checking multiple feature gates wherever the extension feature is used, I propose:
1. Codify inter-FeatureGate dependencies, so if feature B depends on feature A, we make this explicit in the feature gate spec, and validate it on startup
    - Only allow a feature to be enabled if all it's dependent features are also enabled. Enforced in [`featureGate.Validate`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9da4b7ecfb60ea484f8e6c89c42e63506571bc68/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/featuregate/feature_gate.go#L304).
    - Only allow a feature to graduate, if all it's dependent features are at least the same level of maturity. In other words, if feature A is beta, feature B can graduate to beta, but it cannot graduate to GA. (What does this mean for deprecation?). Enforced in unit test.
3. Wherever we need to check if feature B is enabled, we only check feature B, and rely on the validation to ensure that feature A is also enabled.

For an example, the new `InPlacePodLevelResourcesVerticalScaling` (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/132919) depends on _both_ `InPlacePodVerticalScaling` and `PodLevelResources`.

/kind feature
/sig architecture
/cc @JoelSpeed @liggitt @jpbetz @siyuanfoundation

issueContext.body:
If the `TokenRequests` field is set in the `CSIDriver` spec, the tokens are generated and funneled from kubelet to driver as part of volume attributes map. The key for the tokens in the map is `csi.storage.k8s.io/serviceAccount.tokens`.  The service account tokens can be used for workload identity in cloud providers. Especially in case of Secrets Store CSI Driver, these service account tokens are used to access external secrets store to get secrets and mount in the volume. 

As these tokens are sensitive information, it doesn't feel right to include these in the volume context map along with pod name, namespace, service account name which are non-sensitive information. There is a dedicated [secrets field in the proto](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/blob/master/lib/go/csi/csi.pb.go#L4063-L4066) which today is being used for `nodePublishSecretRef` that would be more appropriate for tokens.

To provide more context on "why this issue", we had a CVE in the Secrets Store CSI Driver (ref: [CVE-2023-2878](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/secrets-store-csi-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-g82w-58jf-gcxx)) where the service account tokens were logged as part of the GRPC request in the driver. We use the [protosanitizer](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-lib-utils/blob/master/protosanitizer/protosanitizer.go) in the driver to sanitize the requests before logging but given volume context is not really considered a "secret", the tokens were skipped and logged. We got around this by building custom logic for logging in the driver to strip the tokens but this is something every driver would need to do to be careful and not log the tokens. A change could be made in protosanitizer to sanitize this but given volume context is a map, either entire map needs to be marked a secret or sanitizing has to be done on a field by field basis. issueContext.title: Deletion of csi-node-plugin Pod causes driver entry to be removed from CSINode object; kube-scheduler schedules more than driver's allocatable
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

With @plkokanov we hit in our environments the following issue multiple times:
```
% k -n shoot--foo--bar describe po etcd-main-0

Events:
  Type     Reason              Age                 From                     Message
  ----     ------              ----                ----                     -------
  Warning  FailedAttachVolume  35s (x47 over 80m)  attachdetach-controller  AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "pv-shoot--shik--shak-1234" : rpc error: code = Internal desc = Attach volume /subscriptions/<omitted>/resourceGroups/shoot--shik--shak/providers/Microsoft.Compute/disks/pv-shoot--shik--shak-1234 to instance shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 failed with Retriable: false, RetryAfter: 0s, HTTPStatusCode: 409, RawError: {\r
  "error": {\r
    "code": "OperationNotAllowed",\r
    "message": "The maximum number of data disks allowed to be attached to a VM of this size is 16.",\r
    "target": "dataDisks"\r
  }\r
}
```

When we checked, the CSINode object for the corresponding Node was reporting the correct volume attachment limit:
```
% k get csinode shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 -o yaml

spec:
  drivers:
  # ...
  - allocatable:
      count: 16
    name: disk.csi.azure.com
    nodeID: shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5
    topologyKeys:
    - topology.disk.csi.azure.com/zone
    - topology.kubernetes.io/zone
```

According to the Node status and according to the VM state in Azure, it had already 16 disks attached.
```
% k get no shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 -o json | jq '.status.volumesAttached | length'
16

% az vm show -g shoot--shik--shak --name shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5 | jq '.storageProfile.dataDisks | length'
16
```

kube-scheduler wrongly sheduled a Pod with a volume to the `shoot--shik--shak-cpu-worker-etcd-z1-6c956-mhcw5` Node as the Node already had its volume attachments limit reached.

apiChange.description:
Introduced the alpha `MutableSchedulingDirectivesForSuspendedJobs` feature gate (disabled by default), which allows mutating a Job's scheduling directives while the Job is suspended. 
It also updates the Job controller to clears the `status.startTime` field for suspended Jobs.
